subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A container is in the shape of an inverted cone of height 12 cm and radius 6 cm at the top. It is filled with water at the rate of 12 cm³/sec. What is the rate of change of the height of the water level when the tank is filled to 8 cm?

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you would write first, say what you do about the radius, and say what you differentiate with respect to.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write V in terms of h alone
steps.margin_note: First mark. Here the top radius is half the height, so r = h/2. Getting this ratio and using it to remove r is the whole of the first mark; the examiner looks for the line r = h/2.
lines: Given: dV/dt = 12 cm³/sec.  Asked: dh/dt when h = 8 cm.
Let r be the radius and h the height of the water cone at time t.
The water cone and the full cone are similar, so

recall.must_convey: That similar triangles give r = h/2, so V becomes πh³/12 in h alone.
accept: use similar triangles so r is h by two
the radius is half the height in this cone
remove r first and write volume only in terms of h
similar triangles tho r ni h by two ga rasta
substitute r equal to h by two into the cone volume
volume becomes pi h cubed by twelve

steps.why: The question asks for dh/dt, so V must be a function of h only. Differentiating V = (1/3)πr²h as it stands brings in dr/dt, a rate the question never gives.
common_mistakes: Treating the radius as a fixed 6 cm and writing V = 12πh.
Writing r/h = 12/6 instead of 6/12, which doubles the radius instead of halving it.
Differentiating before removing r, which leaves two unknown rates in one equation.
steps.memory_tip: Read the ratio off the FULL cone once: top radius over full height. In this one that ratio is 6/12 = 1/2, so r is half of h at every level.

steps.label: Differentiate and put h = 8
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Differentiate with respect to TIME, then substitute h = 8. The unit cm/sec belongs inside the box — a rate written without its unit is not a complete answer.
lines: Differentiate both sides with respect to time t:

recall.must_convey: That differentiating with respect to t and putting h = 8 gives dh/dt = 3/(4π) cm/sec.
accept: differentiate with respect to time and substitute h equal to eight
twelve equals sixteen pi times dh by dt
the answer is three by four pi centimetres per second
time tho differentiate chesi h equal to eight substitute cheyyali
solve for dh by dt and write the unit
dh by dt is three over four pi

steps.why: Differentiation is with respect to t, so the chain rule attaches dh/dt to the h³ term. Reducing 12/16π to 3/4π costs one line and is expected in the final form.
common_mistakes: Putting h = 8 into V before differentiating, which gives dV/dt = 0.
Dropping the dh/dt factor that the chain rule produces.
Leaving 12/(16π) unreduced, or writing the answer with no unit.
steps.memory_tip: Differentiate first, substitute second — a number put in early has no derivative left to give.

insider_note: Use SIMILAR triangles to write r = h/2 and eliminate r before differentiating — a cone volume with two variables cannot be differentiated in one step. V then becomes πh³/12.
